CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 59-year-old male presenting with upper respiratory infection symptoms that began one week ago after outdoor yard work. Patient reports fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion, specifically when lifting heavy bags of soil during landscaping activities. He denies productive cough but anticipates it may develop. Patient reports feeling slightly warm but attributed it to physical exertion rather than fever. He endorses mild elbow pain and knee discomfort, which he relates to heavy lifting. Patient has received both COVID vaccines. He denies seasonal allergies. Vital signs in office are normal with no fever present.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or other systemic symptoms. Positive for fatigue, shortness of breath with exertion, and musculoskeletal pain in elbows and knees. Denies fever, productive cough, and seasonal allergies.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin (dose to be increased), Lisinopril 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies reported

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient engages in outdoor activities and yard work. Attends barre classes for relaxation with wife. Works during the week with variable weekend schedule. Reports generally good diet with occasional lapses at social gatherings. Does not consistently monitor blood sugar or blood pressure on weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, afebrile
Heart: Strong, regular rate and rhythm
Lungs: Scattered rhonchi bilaterally, clears with cough
Extremities: Mild edema of lower extremities noted
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral elbow tenderness on palpation

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia
Hemoglobin A1c: 8.0 (elevated; goal 6-7)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/Viral syndrome: Likely viral etiology. COVID test ordered to rule out COVID-19. Patient counseled that symptoms should resolve in a couple of days. Prescribed Robitussin for cough. Advised to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed for fever.

2. Depression: Currently managed without medication. Patient reports good control with barre classes and supportive measures. Offered option of medication or psychotherapy referral; patient prefers to reassess in a few months.

3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Hemoglobin A1c elevated at 8.0%. Increased Metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat Hemoglobin A1c ordered in 4 months. Patient counseled on improved diet and glucose monitoring.

4. Hypertension: Well controlled on current therapy. Continue Lisinopril 20 mg daily. Refill ordered. Lipid panel ordered.

Follow-up appointment scheduled in 4 months. Patient instructed to report if symptoms worsen.
